la:noun:Zeno.html:
Zēno or Zēnon, ōnis, m., = Ζἠνων,
the name of several Greek philosophers.
The founder of the Stoic school, a native of Cittium in Cyprus; form Zeno, ; ; ; ; ; ; form Zenon, B. and K.; .—
An Eleatic philosopher of Elea, in Magna Grœcia, ; ; .—
An Epicurean philosopher, the teacher of Cicero and Atticus, ; ; sq.; .—
A Greek emperor in the fifth Christian century.—Hence, Zēnōnĭānus, a, um, adj., of or pertaining to the emperor Zeno, Zenonian: lex,.

senses: to be jealous of; be zealous for
la:verb:zelo.html:
zēlo, āre, v. a., = ζηλόω.
To love with zeal or ardently (eccl. Lat.): populum summo pietatis amore,; .—
To be jealous of: non zeles mulierem sinus tui,.—
To be zealous for: zelat zelum legis,.—Also in dep. form: zelatus est legem. .—Absol.: zelatus est pro Deo suo,.
